messages.subject_clean: Incorrect mouse-over behavior in 'non-NULL' state
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm developing a(n) (IMO) large App in which one ggvisOutput() is a so-called volcano plot. ggvisOutput()'s 'plot_id' for this div is "volcano_plot" in the gist for which the command to launch it should read:
--
> shiny::runGist("176934a2c0e3f4c5e19521ad953ebdca")
--

In the tabPanel("Differential Expression Plots") that hosts this volcano plot, the user can select a different value for "Contrast" using a selectInput(), after which the data to be displayed in the plot should be updated. However, after selecting a different value (that is, when, 'in shiny::observeEvent() terms', the input is not NULL anymore), which data point (i.e., dot) in the plot gets 'highlighted' by an increased marker size upon 'hovering' over a particular data point as well as the information displayed in the associated tooltip are wrong. This is easily seen by comparing the result of hovering over the same data point before and after changing the "Contrast" from the default "C118_HFD" to (for example) "CORT_C118" and then back to "C118_HFD".

I have isolated the volcano plot visualization including the selectInput() to a separate App for debugging, and found that enclosing the ggvis() call in "server.R" in an observeEvent() 'handlerExpr' apparently resolved the problem (in that separate App). However, after having plugged the isolated solution into the full-fledged App I don't get it working there, i.e. the problem as described above is still present.

I tried several alternatives (in the full-fledged App): observeEvent() (which didn't work due to an obvious cause), reactive(), and eventReactive(), all to no avail.

I ran the App with "Client/Server Tracing" as described on "https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/debugging.html", and thereby found some (IMO) remarkable things that might help in resolving the issue, but I'm afraid that I'm unable to interpret the JSON code sufficiently myself. I'll be happy to post snippets (e.g. of Linux's 'diff' output) if desired, and *can* (FWIW) mention at least that the problematic 'mouse-over' and tooltip behavior appeared to be associated with a relatively large proportion of "SEND {"busy":"idle"}" and "SEND {"busy":"busy"}" echoes to the console.

I suspect (without having further knowledge) that the described issues might have to do with 'observers floating around' (with reference to "https://github.com/rstudio/ggvis/issues/254" - aka, a "lapsed listener problem"?) and that this problem gets worse when Shiny Apps grow, but please correct me if I'm wrong.

Thank you in advance for your help.

messages.subject: Re: Reactive dependencies broken - strange behaviour
messages.subject_clean: Reactive dependencies broken - strange behaviour
messages.body_plain:
If you have this:

a <- reactive({
req(input$x)
input$y
})

and input$x is falsy, then execution aborts at the input$x line (a special error object is thrown). No relationship will be established with input$y--until input$x becomes truthy. This is correct because while x is falsy there's no possible way y could ever effect the outcome.

Now if you do this:

a <- reactive({
isolate(req(input$x))
input$y
})

Urk. Since we've isolated the reading of input$x, changing its value to something truthy will not cause the reactive expression to invalidate.

Why are you isolating the read to available_options? Maybe remove that isolate and if the concern is that the observer runs too often, change it to observeEvent(input$in_option, ...)

eventReactive is a great solution here, sure.

Here's an interesting way to tackle the general problem of "I only care if it's falsy" or whatever. I'll use Hadley's shinySignals package: https://github.com/hadley/shinySignals

available_options <- reactive(...) # as you have it currently
has_available_options <- shinySignals::dropRepeats(reactive(
  isTruthy(available_options)
))
selected_option <- reactive({
  has_options <- has_available_options()
  ...
})

In your case I'd just use eventReactive but I thought this was an interesting way to filter down the event stream of available_options to only that which you care about.

The reason you're seeing this is because your Shiny app is in the inst directory, not under R directory. The R CMD check code analyzer only looks at R/.

One quick to get around this would be to make a spurious call to DT somewhere in R/ (like in a function that's not exported or called).

Or the less hacky way is to move your Shiny app (all of the R code) from inst into R. Your startEDM function wouldn't call shiny::runApp on a directory, but instead, return a shiny::shinyApp(ui, server) object. The main difference is that you can't assume anything about the working directory in that case; every time you want to fetch the data files in your inst, you'll have to use system.file. Actually now looking at your code, it looks like you're doing a lot of source-ing of .R files, that would have to be rewritten in a different way (possibly Shiny modules).

messages.subject: Re: Use Variable for observeEvent eventExpr
messages.subject_clean: Use Variable for observeEvent eventExpr
messages.body_plain:
This is scoping problem (by the way, this has to do with general scoping rules for R, not shiny in particular). Since the observers are lazily evaluated, both of those observers exist long after the code in the server has been run. By then, only the last reference to the `addToButton` variable (`addToButton <- "listen2"`) has been kept. There are two common ways around this (both of these capture local variables in a type of closure so that they remain accessible after the code has run):

1) the more quick and dirty type: use `local()`:
>
>
> library(shiny)

> server <- function(input, output, session) {
>
>   observerList <- list()
>
>   observeEvent(input[["add"]], {
>
>     local({

>       addToButton <- "listen1"
>       observerList <<- observeEvent(input[[addToButton]], print(2))

>     })
>     local({

>       addToButton <- "listen2"
>       observerList <<- c(observerList, observeEvent(input[[addToButton]], print(3)))
>     })
>   })
> }
>
> ui <- fluidPage(
>   actionButton("add", "Add Observers"),
>   actionButton("listen1", "Show 2"), # Nothing printed, but 2 should be.
>   actionButton("listen2", "Show 3")  # 2 and 3 printed, although only 3 should be printed.
> )
>
> shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

2) the scalable but more elaborate type: use lapply (or another apply/functional)

> library(shiny)
>
> server <- function(input, output, session) {
>
>   observerList <- list()
>
>   observeEvent(input[["add"]], {
>
>     btns <- c('listen1' = 2, 'listen2' = 3)
>
>     sapply(names(btns), function(name) {
>       observerList <<- c(observerList,
>                          observeEvent(input[[name]], print(btns[[name]])))
>     }, simplify = FALSE, USE.NAMES = TRUE)

>   })
> }
>
> ui <- fluidPage(
>   actionButton("add", "Add Observers"),
>   actionButton("listen1", "Show 2"),

>   actionButton("listen2", "Show 3")

> )

> shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

See this thread to learn more about this: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/532

>

> {
>   observeEvent(input[["add"]], {
>
>     addToButton <- "listen1"
>     observerList <<- observeEvent(input[[addToButton]], print(2))

messages.body_plain:
Hello Shiny community,

I have been thinking about developing a Shiny app for one of my projects (I am an ecologist), in order to allow partners in different locations to visualize the data we collect together. I work with communities in remote locations where there is often limited internet access, and limited bandwidth. I was wondering if anyone has experience with this, and has suggestions on whether Shiny works in these circumstances or whether I should look for an alternative approach?

Thank you!

Hey there Emma,

It seems to be okay in our experience, but a lot of it depends on how much data you will be sending to the client, as well as how much Javascript needs to be downloaded too.

One of our apps sent a large data frame to the client (using DT) and that was noticeable (1MB+). But not a deal breaker.

Prior to the recent versions with the better connection management, however, we did have a bit of a hard time accessing from, for example, a coffee shop. But now it seems significantly better. So make sure you are running the latest version and take advantage of the new connection enhancements.

Maybe others have a bit more insight on it than I do though!

~ Laz Peterson

messages.subject: Re: Configuration for running Apache and Shiny server on port 80 but using different virtual host name
messages.subject_clean: Configuration for running Apache and Shiny server on port 80 but using different virtual host name
messages.body_plain:
Here is what worked for me.
my hostname on Centos 7 is rserver.example.com <http://rserver.example.com>
I added the following lines to the end of my /etc/http/conf/httpd.conf

<VirtualHost *:80>
 ProxyPreserveHost On
 ProxyRequests Off
 ServerName www.rserver.example.com <http://www.rserver.example.com>
 ServerAlias rserver.example.com <http://rserver.example.com>
 ProxyPass / http://localhost:3838/sample-apps/hello/
 ProxyPassReverse / http://localhost:3838/sample-apps/hello/
</VirtualHost>

Restart httpd server i.e. systemctl restart httpd.server
Open firefox and type localhost or rserver.example.com <http://rserver.example.com>
It will go directly to the hello app presented by shiny server

If you want to direct rserver.example.com/hello <http://rserver.example.com/hello> to your shiny app (assuming hello is the name of your app) then change ProxyPass and ProxyPassReverse in the above code to the following
 ProxyPass /hello http://localhost:3838/sample-apps/hello/
 ProxyPassReverse /hello http://localhost:3838/sample-apps/hello/

messages.subject: Re: Error trying to show an image in shiny
messages.subject_clean: Error trying to show an image in shiny
messages.body_plain:
Put the image in a *subdirectory* of the directory where the app code is. The subdirectory must be called "www". Then, use

img(src = "Logo.png")

The reason for "www" is because your app's root directory may contain private files like CSV data, .R files containing proprietary code, etc., so it can't be made downloadable. Instead, we require a separate www subdirectory so by putting a file in there you're specifically asking for it to be made publicly downloadable.

The value of input$ticker is just a string. To lookup the variable with that name, you could (but shouldn't) use get(input$Ticker, inherit=TRUE) or .GlobalEnv[[input$Ticker]]. I don't like that because input$Ticker is coming straight from the (potentially malicious) client and could refer to any variable in the global environment (or any active frame in the case of get()). It's hard to imagine how plotting any arbitrary value could be bad in this case but still feels like a bad code smell to trust an input string so much.

Instead, I would call getSymbol with auto.assign=FALSE and pass the return value to plot. Or if you plan to use showSymbols or whatever later on, then make an explicit environment using new.env(parent=emptyenv()) and pass that explicitly to getSymbol and showSymbols.

messages.subject: Scoping Issue for reactive dataframes
messages.subject_clean: Scoping Issue for reactive dataframes
messages.body_plain:
I'm developing a shiny app in which there are multiple tabs displaying widget-modifiable analyses of a single dataset. In the interest of modularity, I've written scripts for each tab's UI and SERVER code which are sourced within the actual ui.R and server.R scripts. I've also written two global scripts:

- graphs.R which defines functions for displaying analyses
- key_columns.R which defines lists of column names (pairing front and back end names for each column); the lists also separate columns according to which drop-down menus they appear in

I want to create a new tab that displays the dataset and allows the users to apply filters to subset it. In the UI that I created for this purpose, there are two buttons that:
- Apply Filters to subset the dataset; (currently it just replaces the reactiveValue dataframe with a truncated version but the idea is that it will apply user-defined filters to the reactiveValue dataframe)
- Clear Filters return the dataset to its original, full, un-filtered status

The problem is that when the "Apply Filters" button is pressed, it does not appear to have any effect. My best guess is that this is a scoping issue relating to the fact that the ui.R script only gets run once and so even though each tab has dynamic widgets that alter the display of the page based on user-input, the ui.R only ever sees the original version of the dataframe no matter what filters are applied. I suspect that I can solve the problem by either:

- re-writing the app such that each supporting function checks to see if it should apply any filters to the full dataframe
- changing the scoping somehow to make each tab "subservient" to the tab where the filters get applied (which is what I originally thought would be accomplished by using reactiveValues() in concert with observeEvent() )

Am I on the right track to solving this? Am I missing something important?

Here are my ui.R and server.R scripts:

# UI.R
library(shiny)
library(plotly)
library(Cairo)

# SOURCE IN SCRIPTS FOR EACH TAB'S UI
source("pre_UI.R")
source("diff_UI.R")
source("cross_UI.R")
source("selector_UI.R") # THIS IS THE TAB WHERE DATASET FILTERS ARE SUPPOSED TO BE APPLIED

options(bitmapType='cairo')

# DEFINE UI FOR EACH TAB BASED ON FUNCTION DEFINED IN IT'S SCRIPT
pre_ui <- createPreTabUI()
diff_ui <- createDiffTabUI()
cross_ui <- createCrossTabUI()
selector_ui <- createSelectorTabUI()

# HEADER
hPanel <- headerPanel(
  # LOTS OF TEXT, WORKS FINE, NOT RELEVANT TO MY QUESTION
)

ui<-navbarPage("BMS038",
           navbarMenu("Genomics & Outcome",
                      tabPanel("Pre-therapy",pre_ui),
                      tabPanel("Change on therapy", diff_ui)),
           tabPanel("Cross-therapy", cross_ui),

           tabPanel("Select Patients", selector_ui),

           header=hPanel
           )
# Define UI for BMS-038 Companion website

shinyUI(ui)

# SERVER.R

library(shiny)
require(ggplot2)
require(plotly)
require(survival)
require(GGally)
require(grid)
require(gridExtra)
require(plotly)

# SOURCE IN SUPPORT SCRIPTS
source("key_columns.R")
source("graphs.R")
source("pre_tab_logic.R")
source("diff_tab_logic.R")
source("cross_tab_logic.R")
source("selector_tab_logic.R") # THIS IS WHERE THE DATASET FILTERS ARE MEANT TO BE APPLIED

# READ IN FILES
predat = read.csv("pre_data_122016.csv")
# REMOVE ON-TREATMENT SAMPLES
predat = predat[predat$SampleType == "pre",]
# CHANGE myBOR TO FACTOR
predat$myBOR <- factor(predat$myBOR, levels=c("PRCR","SD","PD"), ordered = TRUE)
full_dat = predat
half_dat = predat[1:40,]
preondat = read.csv("pre_vs_on_data_122016.csv") # DIFFERENT DATASET; WILL EVENTUALLY WANT TO ALLOW THIS TO ALSO BE FILTERED

# DEFINE SERVER LOGIC
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  values <- reactiveValues(predat_1 = full_dat)
  # SUBSET DATAFRAME WHEN BUTTON IS PRESSED
  observeEvent(input$set_filter, {
    values$predat_1 <- half_dat
 })
  # RESET DATAFRAME TO ITS FULL, UN-FILTERED STATE
  observeEvent(input$clear_filter, {
    values$predat_1 <- full_dat
 })
  createPreTab(input, output,values$predat_1)
  createDiffTab(input, output, preondat)
  createCrossCorrTab(input, output, values$predat_1)
  createSelectorTab(input, output, values$predat_1)
})

I am happy to share code from the support scripts as needed; just wanted to avoid overwhelming you with too much at first in case there are crucial issues apparent in these two scripts.
